stem: Kailani drew four congruent squares. She shaded the same fraction of each square. This is one of Kailani's squares.
instruction: Which square CANNOT be another one of Kailani's squares?

options.label: F
options.text: A square with eight equal rows and one shaded top right small square (1/8 shaded).

options.label: G
options.text: A square divided into four smaller squares, each divided diagonally into two triangles, with one large bottom-left triangle shaded (1/8 shaded).

options.label: H
options.text: A square divided into four smaller squares, each divided diagonally into two triangles, with one small top-left triangle shaded (1/8 shaded).

options.label: J
options.text: A square divided into four rows and four columns (16 small squares), with one shaded in the second column, second row from the top (1/16 shaded).

visual_elements: One large square divided into 8 equal horizontal rows with the top row shaded.
Option F: A square divided into 8 equal horizontal rows and 2 equal vertical columns with the top right small rectangle shaded.
Option G: A square divided into 4 smaller squares, each divided diagonally into two small triangles, with the bottom-left large triangle shaded.
Option H: A square divided into 4 smaller squares, each divided diagonally into two small triangles, with the top-left small triangle shaded.
Option J: A square divided into 4 horizontal rows and 4 vertical columns with one small rectangle shaded in the second column, second row.
difficulty_rationale: Requires understanding of fraction equivalence and visual fraction comparison, involving reasoning about shape partitioning and equal fractions.
